title: Services
description: Six things we do, and what you get from each: what arrives, how long it takes and roughly what it costs.

props.title: Six things we do, and what you get from each
props.subtitle: Most agency service pages list disciplines — strategy, design, development. That describes our org chart, not your outcome. Below is what arrives, how long it takes and roughly what it costs.

items.title: Brand identity
items.description: For companies whose look no longer matches what they sell — usually after a pivot, a funding round or a new audience.
points: Positioning statement and messaging matrix
Wordmark, symbol, type and colour system
Applied to website, product UI and deck
Figma library and CSS variables

items.title: Website design and build
items.description: When the brand is fine and the site is what is losing you deals. We design it and we ship it — no handover to a third party who never saw the thinking.
points: Message testing with five of your customers
6–12 page designs, responsive
Built in Astro, handed over as a repo
Analytics and conversion events configured

items.title: Product UI design
items.description: The screens people use every day, not the ones in the sales deck. We work inside your repo and your constraints, with your engineers.
points: Audit of what exists, with the greys counted
Core flows redesigned, every state specified
Component set your engineers accepted
Accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA, tested

items.title: Design system
items.description: For teams rebuilding the same button four ways. The hard part is adoption, so half the engagement is spent on that rather than on components.
points: Tokens in Figma and in code, in sync
Components with every state, documented
Contribution process and migration plan
Training session with your whole team

items.title: Messaging and copy
items.description: Often the cheapest fix available. Three of our clients got more from rewriting their homepage than from redesigning it, and we said so before taking the money.
points: Customer interviews, recorded and quoted
Homepage and three key pages rewritten
A voice guide with real before-and-after

items.title: Embedded designer
items.description: One named designer inside your team two days a week, for companies not ready to hire. We have twice worked ourselves out of the job by running the hiring loop.
points: Same person every week, in your Slack
Design system maintained, not just used
Monthly written review of what shipped
One month’s notice, either way

props.title: The same five steps, whichever service
props.subtitle: Including what we need from you each week, because that is the part every agency leaves out and every client discovers too late.

items.title: Scoping call
items.description: Thirty minutes, no deck. We say early if we are wrong for it.

items.title: Written proposal
items.description: Scope, price, dates and what is explicitly out. Within three days.

items.title: Discovery
items.description: Five calls with your customers, run by us. Projects turn on these.

items.title: Build, weekly
items.description: Working sessions, not a reveal. A surprise at the end is a process failure.

items.title: Handover + 90 days
items.description: Files, tokens, rulebook, recordings — then a free review three months on.

props.title: Budgets, published
props.subtitle: Publishing these cut our enquiries by a third and raised signed projects. Nobody spends two calls discovering we are three times apart.
props.note: 50% on signature, 50% on handover. Thirty-day terms. We have never charged a change fee we did not warn about first.

props.label: What we turn down
items: **Logo-only projects.** A mark without positioning is decoration, available for a tenth of our fee.
**Pitches against more than three studios.** Free speculative work subsidises clients who have not decided.
**Consumer and packaging.** Not our strength; we will send you two names who are better at it.
**Anything under six weeks.** We would take your money and hand back a worse version of what you have.

items.text: They told us the messaging was the problem, not the design, and quoted a third of what we expected to spend. Demo requests went up 38%.
items.name: Dan Okoye

items.text: The weekly working sessions were uncomfortable and completely right. Nothing at handover was a surprise to anyone.
items.name: Sofia Grimaldi

openSlot.label: Open slot
openSlot.text: Reserved for a quote about the embedded engagement ending in a hire. Empty until someone says it on the record.

items.title: Can we start with something small?
items.description: Yes, and often you should. Messaging at €14K tells both of us a lot before anyone commits to a €70K rebrand. About a third of our large projects started that way.

items.title: Who actually does the work?
items.description: The person named on each service, in every session. No account manager in between, and we do not subcontract without telling you who and why.

items.title: What if we need changes after handover?
items.description: The 90-day review is free and most things get fixed there. Beyond that it is €1,200 a day, quoted before the clock starts.

items.title: Do you sign NDAs and work white-label?
items.description: We sign yours without negotiating it, and we work white-label for three other studios. Portfolio use is always your call and we will hold work back indefinitely.

items.title: What if it is not working out?
items.description: Either side can stop after the two directions in week two. You keep everything produced and owe only the deposit. It has happened twice in seven years, both times correctly.

props.title: Thirty minutes, and you will know if we fit
props.subtitle: You talk to Núria, not a salesperson. If the brief is not ours you leave with two other studios’ names before the call ends.
props.note: Next start date 3 November · two slots left this year · we reply to every brief within two working days
